title: The 10 Best Oscillating Spindle Sanders
subtitle: Benchtop and portable spindle sanders for smoothing curves, arcs and band-saw cuts, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An oscillating spindle sander smooths curved edges (band-saw cuts, cabriole legs, templates) by spinning a sanding sleeve that also moves up and down, so it doesn't burn or groove the wood. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (variable speed, a cast iron table, a belt attachment for straight and convex edges, and a beveling table). Benchtop sanders are the norm; WEN and Triton also make portable ones that clamp upside down. They run from about $56 for WEN's portable HA5932 to $770 for JET's benchtop JBOS-5.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: WEN 6510T 3.5 Amp Oscillating Spindle Sander
products.verdict: The highest-rated and most-reviewed spindle sander here: a 1/2 HP benchtop sander with onboard storage for every spindle and a dust port, for about $104.
products.best_for: Most woodworkers adding their first spindle sander.
products.skip_if: You need a tilting table for bevels; the AT6535 has one.

products.name: WEN HA5932 5-Amp Variable Speed Portable Oscillating Spindle Sander
products.verdict: The cheapest sander here and the most versatile: use it handheld on work too big to lift, or clamp it upside down to the bench, with variable speed, four spindles, clamps and an edge guide.
products.skip_if: You want a dedicated benchtop with a big table.

products.name: Triton TSPS450 3.5Amp Cast Iron Top Oscillating Spindle Sander
products.verdict: A cast iron table for flat, stable sanding, six sleeves up to 3 inches with matching drums and inserts, and onboard storage.
products.best_for: Steadier work on a heavy table.
products.skip_if: You need to sand bevels; the table doesn't tilt.

products.name: WEN AT6535 3.5-Amp Oscillating Spindle Sander with Extra Large Beveling Table
products.verdict: WEN's big-table model: a 14-1/2-inch square table that bevels to 45° for angled edges, five sleeves to 2 inches and onboard storage.
products.skip_if: You don't need bevels; the 6510T is far cheaper.

products.name: Woodskil Variable Speed Oscillating Spindle Sander for Wood, 4A (OSM-1V)
products.verdict: A benchtop sander with variable speed, which few here have, a 4A motor and six sleeves up to 3 inches, at 26 lbs.
products.best_for: Slowing down for hardwood and burn-prone woods.

products.name: Woodskil Variable Speed Oscillating Belt and Spindle Sander, 4x24" Belt
products.verdict: A combo sander with a 4x24-inch belt for convex curves and straight edges plus five spindles, with variable speed and oscillation.
products.best_for: One machine for inside and outside curves.
products.skip_if: You want a track record; reviews are shared with Woodskil's spindle-only model.

products.name: VEVOR Oscillating Belt and Spindle Sander, 2400RPM, 5 Sleeves & 24" x 3.86" Belt
products.verdict: A belt-and-spindle combo with a tilting table, five sleeves, a 24-inch belt and onboard storage, for about $47 less than Woodskil's combo.
products.best_for: A budget combo sander with bevel capability.

products.name: Triton TSPSP650 650W Portable Oscillating Spindle Sander
products.verdict: Triton's portable spindle sander: 650 W with variable speed, quick-change drums, an inverted bench-mounting set, a dust port adapter and an edge guide.
products.best_for: A stronger portable than the WEN HA5932.
products.skip_if: Price matters; the WEN HA5932 does the same job for $94 less.

products.name: RIDGID EB4424 Oscillating Edge Belt / Spindle Sander
products.verdict: The classic belt-and-spindle combo, with ball bearing construction and a 5A motor, made in Taiwan.
products.best_for: RIDGID fans who want the original combo design.
products.skip_if: You want details on the listing; it has very few.

products.name: JET Benchtop Oscillating Spindle Sander, 1/2 HP (JBOS-5)
products.verdict: A shop-grade benchtop: the spindle runs on precision ball bearings with a worm-gear oscillation in a sealed oil bath, on a 14-1/2-inch cast iron table that tilts to 45°.
products.best_for: Professional shops that sand curves daily.
products.skip_if: You're a hobbyist; the WEN 6510T rates higher for a seventh of the price.

avoid.name: RIKON Power Tools 50-300 Oscillating Spindle Sander
avoid.flag: Motor rating contradicts itself; lowest rating
avoid.verdict: A $700 sander with a lower rating and a muddled motor spec. For more money you get JET's sealed gearbox; for far less, the WEN 6510T is rated 4.7.
reasons: It's sold as a 1/2 HP motor but lists a 2.5 A draw. At 120 V that's about 300 watts, roughly 0.4 HP, short of what it claims.
At 3.7 stars it's the lowest-rated spindle sander we compared, at the second-highest price.
The JET JBOS-5 costs $70 more with a sealed oil-bath gearbox, a ball-bearing spindle and a 4.3-star rating.

buyers_guide.a: The up-and-down stroke spreads wear across the whole sleeve and stops the abrasive from cutting grooves or burning the wood, which a plain spinning drum does.

buyers_guide.q: Spindle only or belt and spindle?
buyers_guide.a: Spindles sand inside curves. A belt attachment adds a flat face for outside curves and straight edges. Combo machines save bench space.
Benchtop sanders give a big table that keeps edges square. Portable ones like the WEN HA5932 go to work too big to lift and clamp upside down for bench use.

buyers_guide.q: What grit sleeves should I use?
buyers_guide.a: 80 grit to shape and remove saw marks, 120 to 150 to refine, then hand-sand finer. Match the sleeve diameter to the curve: the largest that fits.
Yes. Spindle sanders throw fine dust. Connect a shop vac to the dust port and wear a dust mask.
